title: Shipping AI to a Million Patients Without an A/B Test — Jared Joselowitz, Ufonia
talk_summary: Ufonia builds a safety/evaluation stack for a clinical voice agent that cannot A/B test on patients, so they replace the ship-watch-rollback loop with LLM-simulated patients (Matrix), an LLM judge validated against clinicians, and automatic prompt optimization (GEPA) against a cost-weighted metric. The transferable core is: manufacture rare failure cases synthetically, grade them with a validated judge, and optimize prompts against that metric instead of hand-tuning.

takeaways.technique: Synthetic adversarial scenario suite with LLM-simulated counterpart
takeaways.what_they_do: An LLM 'patbot' is conditioned on a specific scenario (what the user should try to do) and converses with the target agent, generating thousands of dialogues covering rare/dangerous cases that don't occur naturally.
takeaways.numbers: ~200,000 real calls; thousands of simulated dialogues per iteration

takeaways.technique: LLM judge validated against expert labels, tuned for sensitivity
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a judge that takes the dialogue, expected behaviors, and hazard list, outputs pass/fail plus structured reason; validated it on 240 expert-labeled examples against 10 clinicians and picked the model/threshold that maximizes sensitivity.

takeaways.technique: Automatic prompt optimization (GEPA) against a cost-weighted metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Define a metric/cost matrix, run data through GEPA, have a strong LLM reflect on failures and rewrite the prompt iteratively, keeping the best-prompt frontier until budget is exhausted; replaces hours-to-days of manual prompt engineering with 30-60 min runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: manual prompt engineering would take in the order of hours to days to this is in the hour of minutes
takeaways.numbers: 30 min to 1 hour per optimized prompt; cites formatting changes swinging benchmarks 76 points

takeaways.technique: Cost-matrix metric instead of flat accuracy
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of averaging accuracy, they encode asymmetric costs (missing a red flag = catastrophic, false alarm = mildly annoying) and optimize/report against that, recompiling the prompt when the desired metric changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You give it a cost matrix... higher reward for finding the red flags and a lower reward for um for missing them

takeaways.technique: Staged gated rollout where each stage earns the next
takeaways.what_they_do: Simulation -> user testing -> supervised real evaluation with clinicians in the loop -> monitored deploy, with autonomy increased only as evidence accumulates; every artifact traces back to the hazard it addresses.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Simulation earns the right to to to test on real people... you don't just flip a switch. You cross it in stages

takeaways.technique: Pin prompt versions and keep traces tied to hazards
takeaways.what_they_do: Every call, dataset, pinned prompt, and judge verdict traces back to the exact hazard it addresses; prompt versions are pinned so results are reproducible.
